chapter: Chicago radio, Whiteman and courting Mildred
title: Courtship in Chicago: dinners and hearing Hines and Ellington
summary: He and Mildred begin going out after work to hear Earl Hines, Duke Ellington and others; Ted Pearson and Don Bernard are part of the circle.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Now the thing with Whiteman and this job and that lasted quite awhile.

Well, when -- when Whiteman guys would come down, then did you -- you recognized Frankie Trumbauer, did you know Frankie Trumbauer, then or did you get to know him then. You knew him from having listened to him?
No, I got to know him during that time. Yeah, In Chicago --
I mean you listened to him?
During that time, cause then, I don't know, we did something that band with Mildred, and I forgot what it was, now I don't -- can't put my hand on it. But we did some kind of a little show.
At the Sherman Hotel, I think it was,
-- I forget what it was. And I remember we had dinner at the Sherman.

I said, 'Have you eaten?' She said, 'No.' I said, 'Want to eat?' And she said, 'I haven't eaten.' I said, 'Well you're through singing, you can eat before you go to work.' She said, 'All right, fine.' I said, 'Let's go.' So we ate in the Sherman. And, I don't know we just got to talking. And I used to go out and hear Earl Hines and I knew -- I used to go and hear a lot of people all around town and she seemed to know what was happening as far as the clubs were concerned. We used to -- so we started -- I'd see her on the thing, I said, 'Somebody's in town, Duke Ellington's out at the Dells or something, see? I said, 'Let's go out and hear him.' She said, 'Well, I can't go till after work.' I said, 'Well they're open late.' So, maybe I said, 'Get Mattie, he wants to go too,' I saw Melnick --
-- so then the three of us would go out.
And maybe another night, oh, Ted Pearson
Well, for all our daytime shows.
And the producer of all those shows, I worked, in fact the producer on Victor Young's show. Don Bernard, remember him?
Don Bernard, later was with Estee Advertising Agency, big music fan. And, very good friend of Mildred's. In New York here.
And so we used to go out and then Ted Pearson's the one that gave him the name of Fatha Hines.
